doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Williams on listening and playing too loud
summary: Williams says that if you cannot hear everyone else you are playing too loud, and that music is relative.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I insist that they don’t get a chance to do one thing and that is to listen, and to hear the other musicians that they’re working with.

Everybody’s got a microphone in front of them, you know? With a microphone in front of them, and have a — “well look, I can’t hear my monitor” you know, that type. Everybody’s an engineer. But your monitor — but wait a minute. I start by telling them if you can’t hear everybody else in this organization, you are playing too loud. That’s all there is to it.

And if you can hear, see how you going to relate to what you haven’t heard or what you can’t hear? And music is relative if it’s nothing else. I mean otherwise, you’re just out there blowing and it doesn’t mean anything. It’s not going anywhere, it isn’t saying anything.
